title: No lo puedes probar gratis
body:

No hay prueba gratuita y el cobro es automático, lo cual ya es poco amigable para el usuario.

Me hace mucha gracia porque lo primero que hice fue ponerme en contacto con Apple, la respuesta fue rápida y eficaz, generalmente reembolsan de inmediato, pero en este caso concreto era la app quien debía hacerme el reembolso.


Lo más grave es que en esta app tardaron bastante en responder y su respuesta no aborda el tema del reembolso, solo envían un mensaje genérico. 
Incluso respondiendo por mail tal y como indican mas abajo.  
Muy mala experiencia con el soporte. No lo volveré a utilizar nunca.

title: The Best AI intuitive task manager
body:
After spending countless hours  and days searching for an app that combines voice recognition with AI, that is simple, intuitive, elegant, and that actually works properly, I honestly thought it was almost impossible. I felt like nothing like this existed.

Then I discovered Tiimo, and I was immediately blown away. The floating design feels incredibly smooth and natural, right from the very first introduction and setup. Everything about it is fluid, well thought-out, and a joy to use. 

Finally, here is an AI task manager that truly delivers. The voice recognition is excellent! In my opinion, it completely outperforms well-known apps like Todoist, Tick Tick, or Microsoft To Do.

Congratulations for the designers and the devs!

title: Great but would need UX improvements
body: The way the app is designed is overall great, however, I feel like the UX could be improved quite a bit. For instance, selecting an emoji for a task is laggy, they take a very long time to load. Then, moving a task to the previous day when it’s a repeated one creates a copy of the initial task, making it duplicated. It’s a lot of little things like that, seemingly the app hasn’t been tested entirely. One key feature that I’m missing would be to be able to drag and drop tasks around. Or a way to make it easier to be flexible with the tasks, as my day tends to not go as I initially planned I have to adjust a lot. I was using Trello before, and it was very simple to just move the task to another board, I find that I miss that on this app. Otherwise, it’s overall good and helpful, it just needs a bit of polishing to ensure it’s bug free,

title: App’s too easy to ignore and assumes you did what you planned
body: I like the general layout, but this app has the same problem any day planner has: it’s too easy to forget about. I honestly forgot I had it after less than a week until I got an annual renewal reminder. But, my biggest problem, and what essentially made the app useless for me, is that it automatically marks subtasks in scheduled routines as complete according to the time. What’s the point of a checklist that just assumes you’ve completed your tasks? It might work well for people just on the autism spectrum, I wouldn’t really know, but many ADHDers need triggers and urgency to get things done, which this app doesn’t sufficiently provide. It basically turns into a log of things I didn’t do and just fuels my disappointment in myself.

title: No apta para profesionales
body:
En mi opinión es una buena app que combina calendarios y tareas de una forma visual interesante. Siempre y cuando estés principalmente enfocado a tareas. 

Sin embargo, para profesionales que usamos varios calendarios compartidos la app no sirve. Importa bien los calendarios, pero no permite asignar de forma automática un color en concreto a cada uno. De esta forma es imposible distinguir en un vistazo las tareas de uno y las de grupo. 
Lo mismo pasa con las vistas de calendario. Solamente la de día y el mes entero. 

Lo dicho, para uso profesional no es útil. Me encanta el diseño y el concepto detrás de ella, pero es para gente con un día a día mucho más simple. 

Lo de los que ponen una estrella por lo de la suscripción: nadie os hace pagar nada. Si no entedéis como funciona un período de prueba no es problema del desarrollador…

title: Great app
body:
Great little app from a motivated independent developer team that covers different ground than other timetracking apps. Not everybody wants to become a productivity ninja, maybe they just need a friendly someone helping with reminders and making daily task management a bit easier. Lots of examples in the app, a blog, and a quick and helpful customer support service. They give a two week trial before commiting to subscription. You can cancel the sub from the app itself so there's no hidden catch. 

I loved Tiimo, tried it for a few days but felt that it wasn't for me at this moment, might give it another chance in the future. But I think it can be perfect for many other people, that's why I'm writing this review. Don't get scared by the subscription before trial, as I read it's a common complaint in the reviews. Just try it and see if it works for you.
